  • Added Source SRC-1124: LiveLaw, 19 Oct 2026

entry.content:

  • Edited Question OQ-064: The Delhi Police Commissioner's standing order of 11 October 2026 de-notifying Jantar Mantar as a protest site: its text, its date of issue and publication, the legal power it cites, the three replacement venues, and the revised SOP for protests said to follow. entry.title: 264 records added
entry.content:
Add 13 incidents from 2014, 2015 and 2022 with 152 evidence items

  • Added Incident INC-0049: Police water cannon on ABVP and NSUI students at Delhi University
  • Added Incident INC-0050: Police action against UPSC CSAT protesters in Delhi
  • Added Incident INC-0051: Lathicharge and water cannon on the SFI march to the Vidhan Sabha
  • Added Incident INC-0052: Police action on University of Kashmir students protesting a classmate's arrest
  • Added Incident INC-0053: Lathicharge on Presidency College students demanding union elections
  • Added Incident INC-0054: Baton charge on students protesting offline board exams
  • Added Incident INC-0055: Lathi charge on protesting students at Bangalore University
  • Added Incident INC-0056: Lathicharge and tear gas at hijab-dispute protests in Karnataka
  • Added Incident INC-0057: Police stop Aliah University students marching after a student leader's death
  • Added Incident INC-0058: Police detain students protesting offline exams at Delhi University
  • Added Incident INC-0059: Students detained outside Delhi Police headquarters after the JNU Kaveri Hostel clash
  • Added Incident INC-0060: Police stop Panjab University students marching to Punjab Raj Bhavan
  • Added Incident INC-0061: Police action against Agnipath protesters in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-001: On Saturday 21 June 2014, during an Academic Council meeting at Delhi University, ABVP and NSUI students who marched to the Vice-Chancellor's office in North Ca
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-002: Injuries on 21 June 2014: Deccan Herald reports two ABVP and four NSUI members injured, so six in total; The Indian Express reports 'a few' ABVP members injured
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-003: Five ABVP members were detained by Delhi Police on 21 June 2014. Deccan Herald states it as its own report; The Indian Express attributes the figure to ABVP pre
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-004: Allegation about who requested the force, 21 June 2014: ABVP Delhi state secretary Saket Bahuguna told IANS 'The administration asked police to do this', and NS
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-005: Deccan Herald reports that on 21 June 2014 'cops videotaped every negotiation, a call for peaceful march, with the student and teacher groups to keep as evidenc
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-006: On Thursday 26 June 2014, about 25 to 30 AISA students were detained near Central Secretariat metro station in Delhi around 11:30 AM as they tried to march to R
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-007: On 26 June 2014 ABVP, INSO and KYS members held demonstrations outside Vice-Chancellor Dinesh Singh's residence demanding FYUP rollback; police presence was inc
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-008: Records to request for 21 June 2014: Delhi Police control-room and PCR logs, any deployment order and requisition for the water cannon, the Station House Office
  • Added Evidence HIST-FYUP14-009: Records to request for 26 June 2014: the prohibitory order covering the Central Secretariat / Rashtrapati Bhavan area (issuing officer, section, date), the dete
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-001: On the evening of 24 July 2014, about 700 civil services aspirants gathered on National Highway 1 between Gandhi Vihar and Wazirabad in north Delhi. Delhi Polic
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-002: Delhi Police say they lobbed tear gas shells to disperse aspirants on NH-1 on the night of 24 July 2014. This is the Tribune's report of the police account, not
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-003: Aspirants and members of the Rajya Sabha alleged that police lathicharged students on the night of 24 July 2014. An aspirant told the Tribune that police stoppe
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-004: On 26 July 2014 the Aam Aadmi Party released photographs of students it said were injured in Mukherjee Nagar on the night of 24 July and demanded a judicial pro
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-005: A case was registered at Timarpur police station in north Delhi under unspecified Indian Penal Code sections over the violence of 24 July 2014. Gulf News report
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-006: On 25 July 2014, police detained civil services aspirants who tried to march to Parliament against the CSAT. Additional Commissioner of Police (New Delhi Distri
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-007: Sources differ on how many aspirants were detained on 25 July 2014: the Tribune reports 'more than 200' and an Additional Commissioner of Police's figure of 235
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-008: Detained aspirants alleged on 25 July 2014 that police beat them; Additional CP Tyagi denied it. One detained aspirant told reporters they were taken to the pol
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-009: The Tribune reports, in its own voice and not as a quotation, that the 25 July 2014 marchers 'had violated Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by marc
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-010: On 25 July 2014 the Rajya Sabha was disrupted over the CSAT. Minister of State Jitendra Singh made a statement in the House that the three-member committee shou
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-011: On 28 July 2014 aspirants protested outside the UPSC office; police put up barricades and took protesters away in a bus. IANS says police detained 'about 40' an
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-012: IANS reports that on 28 July 2014 police used water cannons to disperse aspirants outside the UPSC office before detaining about 40. The PTI report in the Tribu
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-013: On 30 July 2014 in the Rajya Sabha, Sharad Yadav said that children who had been on hunger strike had been 'picked up' by the government side. The Official Repo
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-014: Adjacent events outside the 24 to 28 July window. Deccan Herald (published 2 August 2014) reports that a 22-year-old Manipuri youth was beaten with batons by tw
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-015: Lead outside the window: Oneindia (15 July 2014) says 'several civil services aspirants' were lathi charged by Delhi Police the day before for protesting agains
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-016: Who ordered what is not established. No source read names the officer who ordered the crackdown on 24 July, the Section 144 order or its issuer on 25 July, the
  • Added Evidence HIST-CSAT14-017: Parliament question or answer on police action against CSAT protesters in July to August 2014: none found.
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-001: On 18 March 2015 SFI activists protesting against RUSA, a fee hike and the deferment of Students Central Association elections marched from Panchayat Bhawan to
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-002: The Tribune reported 24 people injured, including policemen and students, and one fire tender damaged. Police said six police personnel, including a woman const
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-003: Police registered a case of rioting and damage to public property under IPC sections 147, 148, 149, 109, 188, 353 and 352 and Section 3 of the Prevention of Dam
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-004: Six SFI activists, including state president Puneet Dhanta, were arrested on charges of rioting and lawlessness, and a Shimla court rejected their bail on Frida
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-005: The CPI(M) says police broke into its Himachal state office in Shimla about three hours after the clash, taking away staff and SFI national president Sivadasan,
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-006: The CPI(M) names three police officers, a DSP Shimla, an SHO of Boileauganj and an ASI, with about 30 policemen some in plain clothes, as leading the entry into
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-007: The CPI(M) said Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh claimed the students met him at 10 am carrying stones in their bags and pelted police afterwards; the party calle
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-008: The CPI(M) state committee demanded a judicial inquiry by a sitting High Court judge, rejecting a magisterial inquiry, and sought action against named police of
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-009: The CPI(M) leader and Shimla Deputy Mayor Tikender Singh Panwar, quoted by the Tribune, said the police attack on party activists in the office was 'at the behe
  • Added Evidence HIST-SHM15-010: UNKNOWN: who gave the order for the lathi charge and water cannon, whether permission or a prohibitory order covered the Vidhan Sabha march, and who authorised
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-001: On 25 June 2015 a protest at the University of Kashmir, Srinagar, over the arrest of an English Department student turned violent and police fired aerial shots
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-002: Police said the arrested student (named in the sources, and not named here), was arrested for links with militants and was wanted in a case under FIR number 90
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-003: A lawyers' body (the Kashmir Bar, per Kashmir Life) alleged that the vice-chancellor permitted the university police to fire gunshots in the air and let them be
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-004: The university's official handout, quoted by the Tribune, says the vice-chancellor took up the matter with the state Chief Secretary, the Director General of Po
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-005: Students alleged to the Tribune that there was firing inside the campus and that the university authorities looked on; a member of the Kashmir University Studen
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-006: A student participant told Scroll the students had gathered peacefully outside the vice-chancellor's office and that the situation turned violent when 'the secu
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-007: SP Hazratbal Rayees Bhat visited the campus on 25 June to pacify the students, according to the Tribune; his efforts did not succeed. Police separately said the
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-008: The university suspended class work till 27 June and asked hostellers to leave; Scroll reports gates locked on Friday 26 June with hundreds of policemen outside
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-009: Kashmir Life reports the Kashmir lawyers' body condemned police use of force against KU students and demanded immediate release of the arrested student.
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-010: Following the Thursday events, Srinagar observed a complete shutdown on Saturday 27 June 2015 against alleged police atrocities at Jamia Masjid and Kashmir Univ
  • Added Evidence HIST-KU15-011: No permission or prohibitory order (Section 144 / CrPC), no named order-giver for the use of force, no FIR over the campus clash, no inquiry, NHRC or court reco
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-001: Police lathicharged students of Presidency College, Chennai, on Monday 12 October 2015 on Kamarajar Salai, after a protest demanding college union elections. De
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-002: Injury count is disputed: Deccan Chronicle reports 'according to students as many as 20' were injured and treated at Government Stanley Hospital; The News Minut
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-003: Deccan Chronicle reports students stoned an MTC bus and a police patrol vehicle, damaging them, and 'allegedly assaulting police personnel'; police say a traffi
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-004: Triplicane Assistant Commissioner M. Peer Mohammed said on record: 'We had to use minimum required force to control the situation.'
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-005: Arrests: a senior police officer, unnamed, said 'Two post graduate students were arrested. A few others are likely to be arrested.' Police booked students under
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-006: The protest arose from a demand for student union elections. Per Deccan Chronicle, students said they had demanded elections since August and held silent protes
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-007: The News Minute, citing the New Indian Express, reports the Presidency College management had been avoiding elections despite the Lyngdoh committee recommendati
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-008: Whether the principal or college management called the police: neither source says so. Deccan Chronicle reports the college declared a holiday and closed the ga
  • Added Evidence HIST-PCC15-009: Records to request: FIR and charge sheet (Triplicane or the local station), Greater Chennai Police control-room log and deployment orders for 12 October 2015, S
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-001: On 31 January 2022 hundreds of students, described as Class 10 and 12 students, protested at Ashok Mill Naka in Dharavi, Mumbai, near the residence of School Ed
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-002: Police said the students had no permission to protest and had gathered from Mumbai, Thane and Nashik on information shared on social media. DailyO reports the p
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-003: Injuries and detentions. An officer told PTI/FPJ: 'No student was injured in the lathicharge. Some of them were brought to the local police station and released
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-004: DCP Zone V, Mumbai, Pranay Ashok, said on the day: 'We tried convincing & dispersing them' (ANI post, 31 January 2022, as embedded by Careers360), and 'The acti
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-005: An FIR was registered at Dharavi police station against YouTuber Vikas Fhatak ('Hindustani Bhau') and others, and he and one other man were arrested on 1 Februa
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-006: Maharashtra Home Minister Dilip Walse Patil ordered a police inquiry into the 31 January protests. FPJ: he 'had ordered an inquiry by the police department'. Ca
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-007: In Nagpur around 100 students protested near a mall at Medical Square on 31 January 2022. DCP (Zone 4) Gajanan Rajmane said windshields of a city bus and a scho
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-008: Opposition leader Pravin Darekar (Leader of the Opposition in the state legislative council) criticised the police lathicharge on protesting students and said t
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-009: Vikas Fhatak was produced before a Bandra magistrate court and remanded to police custody; the Dharavi police prosecutor Prasad Joshi called him a habitual offe
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-010: UNKNOWN: who ordered or authorised the baton charge at Ashok Mill Naka. No page read names an order-giver; the only named officers are DCP Zone V Pranay Ashok (
  • Added Evidence HIST-BRD22-011: UNKNOWN: outcome of the Home Minister's ordered inquiry. No page read reports the findings, whether a report was submitted, or any action against police or orga
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-001: On the morning of Monday 31 January 2022, Bengaluru city police used lathis on protesting students at the Jnanabharathi campus of Bangalore University. Deccan H
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-002: Two student groups were protesting at the campus. The ABVP protested delay in issuing marks cards, which Deccan Herald described as almost two years. The Bangal
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-003: Deccan Herald quoted ABVP member Tejas Reddy: 'There was another protest led by a different students' organisation and they wanted us to call off our protests.
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-004: Deccan Herald reported student leaders as saying several students, especially women, were severely hurt and hospitalised, and that one female student was bleedi
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-005: Police said none of the groups had sought the permission required to hold a protest. BW reported police saying they tried to convince ABVP members to leave, off
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-006: On Tuesday 1 February 2022 about 300 students gathered near the administrative block to condemn the lathicharge, and submitted a memorandum to the vice-chancell
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-007: ABVP's Bengaluru regional secretary Bhuvan Gowda said, as quoted by Deccan Herald: 'Instead of considering such demands, the vice-chancellor instigated the poli
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-008: SabrangIndia's December 2022 compilation of ABVP-related incidents includes this event, repeating the Deccan Herald wording that police used violence to control
  • Added Evidence HIST-BU22-009: No source read names who ordered or authorised the lathi charge at the campus. The only attributed claim is ABVP's allegation against the vice-chancellor. Polic

  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-003: The Quint reported that eight students were detained in Shimoga and 'as many as 20 people' in total were detained on 8 February 2022, and that Section 144 CrPC
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-004: Prohibitory orders under Section 144 CrPC were put in force in Shivamogga city for 8 and 9 February 2022, banning assembly of five or more people in public plac
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-005: Davanagere district police fired tear gas shells and carried out a baton charge at the Harihar First Grade College campus on 8 February 2022, and Section 144 wa
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-006: Deccan Herald reported that Davanagere SP C B Rishyanth and in-charge IGP (Eastern Range) N Satheesh Kumar inspected the Harihar college on Wednesday 9 February
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-007: Bagalkot district (Banhatti / Rabakavibanahatti, Government Pre-University College): two groups of students threw stones at each other on 8 February 2022. Wheth

  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-009: Bengaluru Police Commissioner Kamal Pant, signing as 'Commissioner of Police and Additional District Magistrate, Bengaluru City', issued an order under Section
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-010: Commissioner Kamal Pant extended the Bengaluru 200-metre prohibitory order by an order dated Monday 7 March 2022, to 22 March 2022.
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-011: The Karnataka government's Advocate General told the High Court on 10 February 2022 that there were counter-agitations by students seeking entry in saffron and
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-012: On 10 February 2022 a three-judge Special Bench of the Karnataka High Court (Chief Justice and two judges, initials CJ, KSDJ, JMKJ on the order) requested the S
  • Added Evidence HIST-HJB22-013: No fetched source names who ordered the lathi-charges in Shivamogga, the tear gas and baton charge at Harihar, or the Raichur detentions, and none names the mag
  • Added Evidence HIST-ALU22-001: On 19 February 2022 about 500 Aliah University students marching with candles from the campus towards Entally were stopped at a police barricade near Padmapukur

entry.title: 330 records added
entry.content:
Add twelve more cases (2014 to 2026) as INC-0016 to INC-0027

  • Added Incident INC-0016: Police entry at Jadavpur University after a gherao
  • Added Incident INC-0017: Police action during the FTII strike
  • Added Incident INC-0018: Occupy UGC: detentions and lathi charges
  • Added Incident INC-0019: Police clearance of the Marina Beach Jallikattu protest
  • Added Incident INC-0020: Police action after the Ramjas College clash
  • Added Incident INC-0021: Police force on Panjab University students
  • Added Incident INC-0022: Shooting near Jamia during an anti-CAA march
  • Added Incident INC-0023: Police action against railway recruitment exam aspirants
  • Added Incident INC-0024: Firing at Secunderabad station during the Agnipath protest
  • Added Incident INC-0025: Detentions and force at the NEET-UG 2024 protests
  • Added Incident INC-0026: Water cannon and lathicharge on BPSC aspirants in Patna
  • Added Incident INC-0027: Lathicharge on teacher-recruitment aspirants in Patna
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-001: Kolkata Police entered the Jadavpur University campus in the early hours of 17 September 2014 (about 2:00 a.m. per one report) to end a students' sit-in or gher
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-002: Who requisitioned the police. The interim Vice-Chancellor of Jadavpur University is reported by DNA to have said he was 'forced to call the police' after demons
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-003: Conflict over whether the Vice-Chancellor took the decision to call police onto campus. (a) DNA, Global Voices and the students: the VC called the police. (b) T
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-004: Which office authorised or directed the specific use of force inside the campus (lights switched off, alleged baton blows, arrests) is not established by any do
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-005: Whether the state government or a minister gave any direction for the police action. The Change.org petition alleges the state government gave a 'green signal'.
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-006: DNA reported that an Additional Commissioner of Police led a strong contingent to the campus at about 2:00 a.m. on 17 September 2014.
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-007: Police and some media accounts held that only minimal force was used. Wikipedia reports the Kolkata Police position as 'minimum lawful force' to escort the Vice
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-008: Arrests on the night of 16 to 17 September 2014: the count is reported as 35 (Gulf News/PTI, released on personal bonds), 36 (Global Voices; the petition says 3
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-009: Injuries on 17 September 2014. DNA reports that a couple of students were in critical condition, one in the ICU of a nearby hospital and another needing surgery
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-010: The molestation complaint behind the protest reached police in early September 2014: a student's father lodged a police complaint with police (2 September 2014)
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-011: Whether a public interest litigation was filed in the Calcutta High Court over the police action, and what the court ordered.
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-012: Whether the West Bengal government constituted a panel to look into the police action, and whether any inquiry report on the 16 and 17 September events was publ
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-013: Outcome for the Vice-Chancellor: The News Minute reported on 14 January 2015 that the Vice-Chancellor announced his resignation on Monday 12 January 2015, calli
  • Added Evidence HIST-JU14-014: No criminal case, departmental action or court finding against any police officer or university official for the events of 17 September 2014 was found in the so
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-001: Students of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, boycotted classes from 12 June 2015 in a strike against the appointment of Gajendra Chauhan
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-002: Pune Police entered the FTII campus after midnight on the night of 18 to 19 August 2015 and arrested five students. The Tribune (PTI) and Ummid (IANS) both repo
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-003: Timing of the police entry is DISPUTED. The Tribune (PTI) says the director went to police at 9:30 pm on 18 August 2015 and police reached the campus about an h
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-004: Who gave the order for police to enter the FTII campus and arrest students on the night of 18 to 19 August 2015: NOT ESTABLISHED. Reports say the director, Pras
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-005: Whether the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting directed the institute's director or Pune Police to call the police or make arrests: NOT ESTABLISHED. Free
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-006: The FIR on the director's complaint: The Tribune (PTI) quotes DCP T Tushar Doshi as saying 'FIRs have been filed against 15 students out of which five have been
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-007: The FIR was reported to include Indian Penal Code sections 143, 147, 149, 323, 353 and 506 'etc.', described as covering unlawful assembly, rioting and criminal
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-008: The five arrested students were produced before a Pune magistrate on 19 August 2015 and were released on bail the same day. Ummid (IANS) reports they were reman
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-009: On 11 March 2016 PTI reported that police had named 18 more FTII students in the gherao case, bringing the total named to 35. Of the 17 earlier named, five were
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-010: Whether the students confined and harassed the director on 17 August 2015 is DISPUTED. The director, Prashant Pathrabe, says he was held in 'illegal confinement
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-011: Injuries and force in the August 2015 campus operation: no injury count and no report of baton use were found in the sources read. Gulf News (IANS) quotes the d
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-012: An Information and Broadcasting Ministry panel report on the FTII situation, reported by the press to say that the director was entitled to call the police and
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-013: On 3 July 2015 police detained students protesting outside the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting at Shastri Bhavan, New Delhi, against Gajendra Chauhan's
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-014: Who ordered the detentions at Shastri Bhavan on 3 July 2015: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Tribune quotes an unnamed official: 'This is to ensure that the protest does n
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-015: A further Delhi protest outside Shastri Bhavan, said to have led to 12 students being detained, was mentioned in a search result attributed to a HuffPost India
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-016: Final outcome of the criminal case arising from the 17 August 2015 gherao (charge sheet, trial, withdrawal, discharge or acquittal): not found in any source rea
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-017: On 7 January 2016, when Gajendra Chauhan formally took charge as chairman, Pune Police detained FTII students protesting outside the campus and used force. The
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-018: Who gave the order to use force and detain students on 7 January 2016: NOT ESTABLISHED. Deputy Commissioner of Police Tushar Joshi, Pune, is reported as defendi
  • Added Evidence HIST-FTII-019: A Supreme Court public interest petition by advocate Vineet Dhanda was reported on 2 September 2015 asking the Court to intervene in the standoff between the Ce
  • Added Evidence HIST-UGC-001: Students from Delhi universities began an 'Occupy UGC' protest outside the University Grants Commission office in New Delhi on 21 October 2015, after the UGC's
  • Added Evidence HIST-UGC-002: Police took roughly 100 protesting students from the UGC office to Bhalswa (Bhalaswa Dairy) police station. The date and the count are DISPUTED. PUDR (2 Novembe
  • Added Evidence HIST-UGC-003: Police used lathis on students sitting outside UGC gate number two on 23 October 2015, according to Amar Ujala, which says several students and police personnel
  • Added Evidence HIST-UGC-004: On 27 October 2015 police at the UGC office lathicharged and detained protesters and took them to Kamla Market police station. Counts conflict. JNUSU's presiden
  • Added Evidence HIST-UGC-005: The deputy commissioner of police (Central) of Delhi Police publicly said that no one had been lathicharged at the 27 October 2015 protest and that protesters h
  • Added Evidence HIST-UGC-006: From the first days the UGC office was under heavy police presence. An AISA leader describes a 'state of near siege' on 21 and 22 October 2015. JNUSU's presiden

entry.title: 286 records added
entry.content:
Add seven earlier cases (2016 to 2024) as INC-0009 to INC-0015, ordered newest first

  • Added Incident INC-0009: Police entry at JNU and the assault at Patiala House Court
  • Added Incident INC-0010: Police on the University of Hyderabad campus; students and faculty detained
  • Added Incident INC-0011: Lathicharge on women students at Banaras Hindu University
  • Added Incident INC-0012: Police and RAF on the Jamia Millia Islamia campus, including the library
  • Added Incident INC-0013: Police action at Aligarh Muslim University and the Aligarh internet suspension
  • Added Incident INC-0014: Masked attack at JNU and the question of police inaction
  • Added Incident INC-0015: Lathicharge, tear gas and water cannon at the Nabanna march
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-001: FIR No. 110/2016 was registered at Police Station Vasant Kunj North, Delhi, over the event held at Jawaharlal Nehru University on 9 February 2016. The Delhi Hig
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-002: The FIR was registered on 11 February 2016 against unidentified persons following complaints from a Member of Parliament of the BJP (named in the report as Mahe
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-003: In the Delhi High Court on 2 March 2016 the Additional Solicitor General for the State submitted that: permission for a cultural evening at Sabarmati Dhaba, JNU
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-004: Kanhaiya Kumar, president of the JNU Students' Union, was arrested by Delhi Police on 12 February 2016 in connection with the sedition case, and was in police c
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-005: Delhi Police went onto the JNU campus on 12 February 2016 and took Kanhaiya Kumar into custody there.
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-006: A letter dated 11 February 2016 from the JNU Registrar to the Deputy Commissioner of Police, South District, is reported to have said that the Vice-Chancellor g
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-007: On 22 February 2016 Delhi Police were reported to be waiting outside the JNU campus for the Vice-Chancellor's permission before entering to arrest students who
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-008: Who gave the order for Delhi Police to enter the JNU campus on 12 February 2016, and who gave the order to arrest Kanhaiya Kumar, is not established by any docu
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-009: The Delhi High Court (Pratibha Rani J.) granted Kanhaiya Kumar interim bail for six months on 2 March 2016 on a personal bond of Rs 10,000 and one surety, prefe
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-010: On 15 February 2016, at Patiala House Courts Complex, New Delhi, people described in reports as lawyers or persons in lawyers' robes assaulted students, teacher
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-011: The Supreme Court's order of 17 February 2016 in N.D. Jayaprakash v. Union of India, W.P.(Crl.) 25/2016 (Chelameswar and Sapre JJ.), records that on 15 February
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-012: The number of people injured at Patiala House Courts on 15 February 2016, and their identities and injuries, is not established by any document read for this fi
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-013: On 22 February 2016 the Supreme Court corrected its order of 17 February after the Solicitor General said that on 15 February 2016 Kanhaiya Kumar was not in fac
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-014: The Supreme Court on 17 February 2016 recorded that it deputed six members of the Bar (Kapil Sibal, Rajeev Dhawan, Dushyant Dave, H.P. Rawal, Ajit K. Sinha and
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-015: At about 4 pm on 17 February 2016 the Committee returned and made an oral report; the Supreme Court asked for it in writing. The order records: 'it is reported
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-016: The written report of the Supreme Court's Committee of advocates, a pen drive of the video one member recorded on his phone, and other reports were filed in sea
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-017: Members of the Supreme Court's Committee told the Court orally on 17 February 2016 that the police did not do their job at Patiala House Courts. PTI reports Mr
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-018: Delhi Police conduct at Patiala House Courts on 15 February 2016, what officers present did or did not do and on whose instructions, is not established by any d
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-019: The National Human Rights Commission issued a notice on 17 February 2016 to the Union Home Secretary, the Chief Secretary of the Government of NCT of Delhi and
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-020: An NHRC fact-finding team report is reported to have found the assault on Kanhaiya Kumar in the court premises 'organized and pre-planned' and to have recorded
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-021: The Lok Sabha debated 'the situation arising out of recent incidents in institutions of higher education' on 24 February 2016. The record shows members stating
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-022: Delhi Police registered four FIRs over the violence at Patiala House Courts on 15 and 17 February 2016, arrested three lawyers (Vikram Singh Chauhan, Yashpal Si
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-023: Delhi Police filed three chargesheets on 19 July 2016 before Metropolitan Magistrate Snigdha Sarvaria: against three lawyers for the 15 February attack on journ
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-024: The Supreme Court on 26 February 2016 issued notice on a petition by advocate Kamini Jaiswal seeking a Special Investigation Team probe into the Patiala House v
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-025: India Legal reported on 26 February 2016 that the Supreme Court 'directed the Delhi Police to set up an SIT' to investigate the 15 and 17 February violence; Liv
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-026: The Supreme Court dismissed N.D. Jayaprakash's writ petition (W.P.(Crl.) 25/2016) and a connected contempt petition (Contempt Petition (C) 503/2016) on 14 Novem
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-027: Whether any written authorisation was issued for the police presence at Patiala House Courts Complex on 15 February 2016 and who held command of that deployment
  • Added Evidence HIST-JNU16-028: JNU wrote to Delhi Police asking them to take utmost precautions before entering the campus, and police officers told the university they would enter only if ab
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-001: Police were deployed on the University of Hyderabad campus on 22 March 2016, the day Vice-Chancellor Appa Rao Podile resumed charge after leave following the de
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-002: The Registrar's Office notice stated that Prof. Appa Rao Podile 'resumed the charge in the Forenoon of March 22, 2016'.
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-003: Chronology of 22 March 2016 as given by one writer: protesters reached the Vice-Chancellor's residence about 10:30; police arrived about 11:30; RAF and more pol
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-004: Count of persons arrested and charged: police and prosecution accounts give 25 students and 2 faculty members (27 accused); the Newslaundry report of the Gachib
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-005: The Joint Action Committee for Social Justice (UoH) alleged that 36 students including 3 professors were detained about 5 pm on 22 March, beaten in a police van
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-006: The Independent Fact Finding Team alleged that 27 students and 2 faculty members were taken into police vans, beaten and held in undisclosed locations for more
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-007: Injuries: PUDR stated that over fifty students were injured; Newslaundry reported a Deputy Commissioner of Police as saying four police officers were injured by
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-008: Police account as reported: after two warnings police used 'mild force'; students allegedly pelted stones, injuring four officers; a lathi-charge and abuse of w
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-009: The Cyberabad Police Commissioner (reported as CV Anand) said of those arrested: 'They were all produced in Miyapur court and sent to judicial remand.'
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-010: On 28 March 2016 the XXV Metropolitan Magistrate court at Miyapur Court Complex granted bail to 27 accused (reported as 25 students and 2 faculty members), on s
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-011: Two cases were registered at Gachibowli police station against protesting students and two faculty members, with charges reported as vandalism, rioting and crim
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-012: On 25 March 2016 the National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of media reports of an 'emergency like situation in Hyderabad University' and iss
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-013: The replies of the Union HRD Ministry, the Telangana Chief Secretary and the Hyderabad Police Commissioner to the NHRC notice of 25 March 2016, and any NHRC cas
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-014: A writ petition by University of Hyderabad professor Tathagata Sengupta and student P. Adityan led the Hyderabad High Court to direct the Telangana government,
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-015: The State's counter-affidavit in the Sengupta and Adityan petition, and any order disposing of it, were not found.
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-016: Utilities and messes: students said water, electricity and internet were cut and all messes closed from 23 March 2016; a faculty statement says 14 hostel messes
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-017: ORDER QUESTION. The Independent Fact Finding Team interviewed the Cyberabad Deputy Commissioner, an Assistant Commissioner, an Inspector of Police and the Telan
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-018: ORDER QUESTION. The fact-finding interim report alleges that the Vice-Chancellor's return to campus was planned with supporters and triggered the violence, and
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-019: ORDER QUESTION. A Kafila guest post by HCU students states that the CRPF and RAF were 'called in at the behest of the Vice Chancellor Appa Rao'.
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-020: ORDER QUESTION. The Joint Action Committee for Social Justice alleged that police, RAF and CRPF acted 'upon the orders of the Central and state government', and
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-021: ORDER QUESTION. A faculty statement says security staff 'had been ordered to bar outsiders from entering' the campus, without saying by whom, and that the admin
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-022: ORDER QUESTION. The university authorities wrote to Cyberabad police asking it to stop 'media personnel, political groups, external student organisations and po
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-023: ORDER QUESTION. An administration 'task sheet' quoted by two University of Hyderabad students in The Wire assigns an administrative officer to inform three name
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-024: ORDER QUESTION. The Round Table India chronology reports that non-teaching staff complained to police about students entering the bungalow, while private securi
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-025: ORDER QUESTION. The public prosecutor told the Miyapur court that 'the arrest were made by the police in order to control the situation' on 22 March.
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-026: ORDER QUESTION. Who gave the order to bring police and central forces onto the campus and to detain students on 22 March 2016 is not established by any primary
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-027: The Vice-Chancellor had a registered case against him under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act in connection with Rohith Vemula's death, on which, accordi
  • Added Evidence HIST-HCU-028: Procedure after detention: the fact-finding team said those arrested were not produced before a magistrate within 24 hours and that police could have given bail
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-001: Police used force, including a lathicharge, against protesting students at Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi, on the night of 23 September 2017. Press reports
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-002: Students began protesting at BHU after 21 September 2017, when a woman student said she was harassed by three men on a motorcycle inside the campus. Students al
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-003: The Varanasi Divisional Commissioner submitted a report to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary on or about 26 September 2017. As reported by IANS, it said BHU did
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-004: Who gave the order for the lathicharge on the night of 23 September 2017 is not established in any document or report retrieved. No order, police log, magistrat
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-005: On 24 September 2017 journalists protesting in Lucknow demanded action against the Varanasi District Magistrate and the Senior Superintendent of Police 'for ord
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-006: Between 24 and 25 September 2017 the Varanasi district administration and police removed from their posts three additional city magistrates, the station officer
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-007: Reports differ on how many officials were removed. Outlook (25 September 2017) lists three additional city magistrates plus the Lanka station officer and the Bh
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-008: Police registered an FIR against unidentified policemen over the lathicharge of 23 September 2017 and a separate case against over 1,000 students over the viole
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-009: The number of students named in the case differs between reports: over 1,000 (PTI via Outlook and Eastern Mirror, 25 September 2017) and 1,200 unidentified stud
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-010: The number of people injured on 23 September 2017 is not established. Reports say only 'a number of students, including women, and two journalists' were injured
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-011: Detentions reported: 16 detained students were released on the evening of 24 September 2017, per the Lanka station officer quoted by PTI via Outlook. Over 200 S
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-012: Vice-Chancellor Girish Chandra Tripathi denied, as reported on 26 September 2017, that students were lathicharged on campus. He said action was taken against pe
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-013: On 24 and 25 September 2017 the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister ordered a probe and sought a report from the Divisional Commissioner, Varanasi; the Varanasi distri
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-014: The BHU Vice-Chancellor ordered a judicial inquiry led by a retired Allahabad High Court judge, reported on 26 September 2017 after an executive council meeting
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-015: The BHU inquiry committee headed by a former High Court judge released its findings on 25 April 2018, per The Wire's LiveWire. It is reported to have given the
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-016: BHU Chief Proctor O N Singh resigned on 26 September 2017, reported as taking 'moral responsibility' for the molestation of a student and the police violence th
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-017: Vice-Chancellor Tripathi went on leave on 2 October 2017 citing personal reasons, and the BHU registrar was appointed interim Vice-Chancellor on 4 October 2017,
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-018: The National Human Rights Commission sought a detailed report on the incident from the Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police and the Vic
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-019: Aaj Tak reports (25 September 2017) that the Prime Minister and the BJP president spoke to the Chief Minister and asked him to take necessary steps. Outlook say
  • Added Evidence HIST-BHU-020: No Allahabad High Court order, petition or commission report on the BHU events of 21 to 24 September 2017 was found in this research.

  • Added Evidence HIST-JMI-005: Who gave the order to use lathis or other force against students, and who ordered detentions: NOT ESTABLISHED. The Delhi Police action taken report, as reported

  • Added Evidence HIST-JMI-016: Delhi High Court judgment of 5 October 2026 (Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain; reserved 24 July 2026) dismissed the batch of eight writ petitions (lead:
  • Added Evidence HIST-JMI-017: Earlier court steps. Supreme Court order of 17 December 2019 in W.P.(Crl) 370/2019 (Alumni Association, Jamia Millia Islamia University v. Union of India) decli
  • Added Evidence HIST-JMI-018: No disciplinary, criminal or departmental action against any police or RAF personnel for the Jamia campus events has been found in any document read. The Delhi
